title: Portfolio pitch: three automation projects that prove a tech can troubleshoot
summary: Three fictional automation projects framed as portfolio proof that a tech can troubleshoot under pressure.

blocks.title: Three projects, one claim: I can troubleshoot
blocks.body: Alex Rivera (fictional) built this portfolio pitch for a senior tech interview. Each project shows a different troubleshooting muscle: intermittent electrical, sequence logic, and network IO. Steal the structure; replace with your real work.

blocks.title: Projects are fictional
blocks.body: Plant names, metrics, and Alex Rivera are invented for this artifact. Present only work you actually did in real interviews.

items.label: Clear claim: troubleshoot to root cause

blocks.heading: Project 1 — Intermittent e-stop drop on a case packer
blocks.body: Situation: Packer at fictional Clearwater Foods dropped e-stop randomly. Action: Alex logged bus voltage and safety loop continuity, found a cracked conductor in a hinge flex. Result: Fault cleared; added a flex-loop inspection to PM. Proof point: instrumentation before parts roulette.

blocks.heading: Project 2 — Transfer timing race after a die change
blocks.body: Situation: After a die swap, Line B double-hit blanks. Action: Compared encoder counts and PLC permissive bits to the prior recipe; found a leftover offset in the transfer teach. Result: Corrected teach + checklist item "verify transfer points after die change." Proof point: sequence literacy, not just module swaps.

blocks.heading: Project 3 — Cell IO drop every night at 02:10
blocks.body: Situation: Nightly IO freeze on a filler cell. Action: Switch logs showed a broadcast storm when a misconfigured camera NVR rejoined. Result: Segmented the camera VLAN; freeze stopped. Proof point: networks are part of automation troubleshooting.

blocks.heading: Proof matrix
rows: Before/after scope or meter log + PM add
Switch log snippet + VLAN change note

blocks.heading: How to deliver the pitch
items: Open with the claim in one sentence.
Tell each project as Situation → Action → Result in under five minutes.
Show one artifact per project (photo of flex, checklist, redacted log).
Close by mapping their job posting keywords to these three muscles.

columns.name: Confident
columns.detail: "I logged the safety loop and found a cracked flex. Here's the PM change."

columns.name: Fluffy
columns.detail: "I'm a passionate team player who loves automation and synergy."

columns.name: Why it matters
columns.detail: Hiring managers buy evidence of troubleshooting, not adjectives.

blocks.heading: Portfolio check
blocks.prompt: Which project best answers "Tell me about a time you fixed a network-related downtime"?
options: None — invent a fourth on the spot

blocks.heading: Build your three
blocks.body: Write three real STAR cards this week. Alex's structure is the scaffold; your logs are the proof.
